title: SDK surface rollout & propagation strategy: compatibility notes, samples matrix, and staging gate runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
project: SDK Launch: Structured Output + Function Calling + Streaming
description: Purpose: coordinate cross-team steps to roll out the updated SDK surface that supports structured output, function calling, and streaming across hosted and dedicated deployments. This ticket consolidates compatibility rules, sample coverage matrix, staging gate criteria, release notes draft, and a propagation/rollback runbook for SDKs and server API changes. Goal is to give eng, docs, SDK owners, and GTM a single canonical plan to execute the next 3-week staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix populated for all officially supported SDK languages (JS, Python, Go, Java) and mapped to runtime versions and model variants
Canonical sample catalog (per feature: function calling, structured output, streaming) exists in the SDK repo and is linkable from release notes
Staging gate checklist completed by infra and QA for canary in us-east-1 and eu-west-1
Release notes draft approved by Legal and Security, and localization owner has sign-off for en/fr/de
Telemetry/metric hooks to measure downstream contract errors (schema mismatches, function resolution failures, stream disconnects) are instrumented and validated
Rollback criteria and automated fallback (server-side compatibility flag) tested in a dry-run

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SDK surface change may cause schema mismatch with earlier client code -> Mitigation: include opt-in negotiation header and server-side compatibility flag, ship migration guide
Risk: Streaming clients may see higher disconnects during canary -> Mitigation: roll out to 5% traffic initially and monitor connection error rate; enable enhanced retry policies in SDKs
Risk: Function calling semantics different across SDKs -> Mitigation: publish language-specific adapters and run conformance tests in CI
Risk: Docs/sample drift -> Mitigation: require samples to be part of SDK repo and included in release artifact checksum

release_notes_draft: What's new in sdk-2025.03: 1) Structured Output: SDKs now support declarative schema attachments for model responses so developers can validate and deserialize generated content more reliably. 2) Function calling enhancements: explicit resolver hooks and richer error codes to make orchestration with external tools easier. 3) Streaming: lower-latency streaming with improved reconnect semantics and resumable segments. Migration notes: update your client to the new SDK release that includes an opt-in negotiation header. For immediate rollback, server-side 'sdk_v2_surface' flag can be toggled. See samples and migration guide links below.
samples_matrix_summary: Canonical samples are grouped by feature and language. Minimum coverage required before GA: (a) Structured output: schema validation example + roundtrip test (JS, Python, Go); (b) Function calling: simple echo resolver, authenticated resolver, and nested-call flow (JS, Python); (c) Streaming: low-latency chat stream, resumable stream, and server-push example (JS only for initial beta). Each sample must include a one-paragraph 'what it demonstrates' and a simple acceptance test that runs in CI.
staging_gate_runbook: Pre-canary checks: 1) Compatibility matrix reconciled and owner approvals recorded. 2) Smoke tests: endpoint health, token auth, sample end-to-end for each language. 3) Observability: streaming_disconnect and function_resolution_failure events have dashboards and alerts. Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% spaced 24h apart if no critical alerts. Rollback criteria: >0.5% schema-mismatch errors OR >2x baseline streaming_disconnect rate OR 99th percentile p95 latency exceeds SLO for 2 consecutive periods. Rollback steps: flip 'sdk_v2_surface' flag to false, disable new SDK artifact distribution, communicate via #release-notifications channel and runpostmortem.
